title: 33 pre-existing tests/integration failures on origin/main (10 files) — failing and leaking, independent of GH #439
symptom: With BPM_TEST_DB_URL pointing at a healthy running test database, `zig build test-integration` reports 33 failing test blocks across 10 already-wired integration test files. The failures split into two kinds: outright assertion/query failures (reported as `error: '<file>.test.<name>' failed:`) and memory leaks (reported as `leaked N allocations:`). tests/integration/iss202_merge_atomicity_test.zig alone accounts for 8 leaking blocks (TC-ISS-202-03/04/05/06/07/10/INT-01/INT-03).
root_cause: NOT YET DIAGNOSED. Deliberately not investigated under GH #439, whose scope is build-graph wiring. What IS established: these failures are NOT caused by GH #439. Verified by checking out origin/main with the feature branch's changes stashed and running `zig build test-integration` against the same healthy database — the identical 10 files fail there. All 10 are wired into a build target already (they are not part of ISS-0137's 55-file unwired backlog), so they have been running and failing on main.
reproduction:
1. Ensure docker-compose db_test is up and healthy and BPM_TEST_DB_URL is set.
2. git checkout origin/main
3. zig build test-integration
4. Observe 33 `error: '<file>.test.<name>' failed:` / `leaked N allocations:` lines across the 10 files listed in affected_areas.
impact: test-integration is not green on main, so it cannot function as a release gate: a real regression introduced into any of these 10 areas would be indistinguishable from the existing noise. The 8 leaking blocks in iss202_merge_atomicity_test.zig are the most concerning subset — a leak in merge/transaction code is a plausible production defect rather than a test-fixture artefact, and merits triage before the assertion failures.
candidate_resolution: Triage per file rather than as one batch; the ten files span unrelated subsystems (audit chain, task claim, webhook outbox, merge atomicity, idempotency keys, error retry, task guard, timer DLQ) and almost certainly have distinct causes. Suggested order: (1) the iss202 leaks, since a leak is either a real ownership bug in merge code or a fixture that fails to free — both worth knowing; (2) audit_chain_utf8 / audit_iss103, which share the audit chain trigger and may have a single common cause; (3) the remainder individually. Note GH #366 (test-integration-others-internal barrier deadlocks, 40P01) and GH #359 (tenant_default shadow table) are open against this same suite and may explain a subset — check those before diagnosing from scratch.
notes: Discovered while wiring 21 previously-unwired integration test files into tests/integration/main_test.zig under ISS-0137 / GH #439. Once those files compiled, running the suite surfaced this pre-existing failing set alongside them. Filed separately rather than fixed inline per the WF-03 handoff constraint: this is a genuinely distinct defect set from the wiring defect, it is not a regression of the wiring change, and diagnosing 10 unrelated subsystems is far outside the scope of a build-graph fix. GH #439's own acceptance criteria (lint_test_wiring.py exit 0, zig build exit 0, zig build test exit 0) are all met independently of this issue — the Green-Main Gate covers `zig build test`, which is service-free and green; this issue is confined to `test-integration`.
